answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Prism Rule: each identity’s actions are hashed into a per-epoch behavioural vector; admission to the next epoch requires the vector’s similarity to its prior history to exceed a fixed threshold, evaluated through a rotating feature prism that samples different behaviour dimensions each time. Sybils must sustain coherent, non-repeating behaviour across epochs rather than one burst. The velvet cost: attackers pay continuous maintenance labour to keep many identities plausibly consistent, and any mismatch at dawn reset discards accumulated standing.
